day_shape: IDF confirms killing of Hamas Gaza chief Izz al-Din al-Haddad in airstrike, launches first wave of strikes on Hezbollah since extended Lebanon ceasefire, NYT-cited reports of US/Israel preparing renewed Iran war next week, CENTCOM says 78 ships redirected under Hormuz blockade.

threads.label: Hamas Gaza chief killed in airstrike
threads.summary: The IDF confirmed the killing of Izz al-Din al-Haddad, head of Hamas's military wing in Gaza, in a Friday night airstrike on Gaza City, with Hamas reportedly confirming his death and a funeral underway. IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir credited Southern Command, Intelligence Directorate, Air Force and Shin Bet, and ordered alertness against retaliation.

threads.label: IDF strikes Hezbollah in southern Lebanon
threads.summary: The IDF launched a wave of airstrikes on Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, described by Times of Israel as the first such strikes since the extended Lebanon ceasefire, after issuing evacuation warnings for nine named villages. Two Hezbollah operatives were killed at a rocket-launch site, weapons caches were recovered, and two drones were intercepted near Metula and Mount Meron; IRIB cited Lebanon's Health Ministry claiming 18 killed and 124 wounded.

threads.label: Reports of renewed US-Israel Iran campaign
threads.summary: Times of Israel and Jerusalem Post cited a New York Times report, sourced to two Middle East officials, that the US and Israel are preparing to resume joint attacks on Iran as soon as next week as talks stall. Defa Press warned against trusting any "American-Zionist ceasefire," and IRIB cited Le Monde reporting Iran has rebuilt much of its ballistic missile arsenal via underground facilities.

threads.label: Hormuz blockade and Trump China visit
threads.summary: CENTCOM said that as of May 16, 78 commercial ships had been redirected and four disabled under US enforcement of the maritime blockade against Iran near the Strait of Hormuz. Jerusalem Post reported Trump saying Xi agreed Iran must reopen the Strait though China gave no indication it would act; IRIB and Defa Press cast the Beijing trip as yielding no Chinese cooperation on Iran.

threads.label: Iran diplomatic and economic strain
threads.summary: Defa Press reported Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met Iran's Deputy SNSC Secretary Ali Bagheri in Istanbul, and Iraq's Ammar al-Hakim hosted FM Araghchi in Baghdad calling for war against Iran to stop. Iran International described café culture collapsing under economic crisis, while IRIB reported electricity-consumption monitoring of 5,000 Tehran offices and 110,000 litres of smuggled fuel seized in South Khorasan.

threads.label: Regime wartime messaging cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted guidance invoking Ferdowsi to "immortalise the epic of the people" of the "third Sacred Defence," and circulated bank details for livelihood packages to war-affected families in Fars Province. Defa Press and IRIB pushed multiple items on the "third imposed war," including a Judiciary Lawyers Centre vow to pursue cases on behalf of "90 million people" to avenge the "martyred leader."

threads.label: Other Hamas strikes and Gaza casualty figures
threads.summary: The IDF announced the killing of two further Hamas operatives, Khamer Iyad Muhammad Al-Matouq and Khaled Muhammad Salem Jouda, in northern Gaza strikes, identifying both as October 7 infiltrators. Defa Press cited Gaza's Health Ministry putting the cumulative death toll at 72,757 with 172,645 wounded, including 13 killed and 57 wounded in the past 48 hours.

Nazarian, CEO of Tehran Regional Electricity Distribution Company: With the announcement of new working hours, the Tehran Electricity Consumption Monitoring Operation Centre began real-time monitoring of electricity consumption of over five thousand public institutions and executive bodies. It is expected that with the change in working hours, more than 150 megawatts of electricity consumption in the capital during peak hours will be reduced. According to a government cabinet decision, offices are required to reduce their electricity consumption by 30 per cent during office hours and 70 per cent during non-office hours compared to last year. In addition, cooling system temperatures must be set to 25 degrees and must be switched off at least one hour before the end of work. Electricity consumption by offices is being monitored on-site and through monitoring systems.

events.title_en: Le Monde: The US narrative of decisive victory does not align with reports of Iran rebuilding its ballistic missile arsenal
events.summary_en: Le Monde: The US narrative of decisive victory does not align with reports of Iran rebuilding its ballistic missile arsenal. American and Israeli strikes on Iran's missile facilities caused damage, but did not eliminate Iran's missile programme. Iran was able to use its domestic production network and underground facilities to rebuild a significant portion of its ballistic missile arsenal and resume missile production. Estimates show that Iran's missile deterrence capacity has been maintained and claims of complete destruction of this military capability have been exaggerated. The speed of reconstruction also demonstrated that in modern wars, industrial capacity and the ability to rapidly replace equipment play a determining role.
